metadata.analyzed_by: AWS Transform Custom — Agentic Readiness Analysis
metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code with deployable entry point (VB6 Form_Load compiled to Win32 EXE) and persistent data store. Classified as application.
metadata.archetype_justification: Database connections (ADODB to Access .mdb), INSERT operations on Customers table, user-specific data (CreatedBy field). Classified as stateful-crud.

findings.title: No API interface — direct database access only
findings.description: The application exposes no REST, GraphQL, or AsyncAPI interface. It is a standalone VB6 desktop application that connects directly to a Microsoft Access .mdb file on a shared network drive via ADODB/Jet OLEDB. Integration requires direct database access or UI automation.
findings.gap: No API layer exists. Agent integration would require either direct database manipulation (brittle, non-auditable) or UI automation (fragile, unscalable).
findings.recommendation: Create a thin REST API layer in front of the Access database to expose customer CRUD operations as HTTP endpoints.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Create a thin REST API layer in front of the Access database
blocker_remediation.target_state: RESTful API with documented endpoints for customer CRUD operations

findings.title: No machine identity authentication
findings.description: The application has no authentication mechanism. It relies entirely on the Windows username (Environ("USERNAME")) for identity attribution and Windows SMB file share permissions for access control. No OAuth2, API key, mTLS, or any machine identity support exists.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication. An agent cannot authenticate to this system with attribution.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a service layer with OAuth2 client credentials or API key authentication.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Introduce a service layer with OAuth2 client credentials
blocker_remediation.target_state: Machine identity authentication with principal attribution in audit logs

findings.title: No audit logging for write operations
findings.description: No audit logging exists. Errors are swallowed with On Error Resume Next and shown to users via MsgBox only. There is no CloudTrail, no structured logging, no log storage, and no immutable log configuration. Write operations (INSERT into Customers) are completely unaudited.
findings.gap: No audit trail for any operation. Agent-initiated writes cannot be attributed, traced, or forensically reviewed.
findings.recommendation: Implement structured audit logging for all write operations with immutable storage (CloudTrail + S3 Object Lock).

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled AND no audit logging exists
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: AUTH-Q6 resolved as BLOCKER because agent_scope is write-enabled and the system has zero audit logging — write operations are completely unattributed.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Implement structured audit logging for all write operations
blocker_remediation.target_state: Immutable, tamper-evident audit logs with agent identity attribution

findings.title: No scoped permissions — single shared database password
findings.description: No authorization model exists. The application uses a single shared database password for all users. All users have identical full read/write access to the entire database.
findings.gap: No scoped permissions mechanism. Cannot grant an agent read-only access to specific resources.
findings.recommendation: Implement role-based scoped permissions in the new API layer.

compensating_controls: Implement read-only database views for agent consumption
Use a middleware proxy that enforces operation-level restrictions

findings.title: No action-level authorization
findings.description: No action-level authorization exists. Any user who can access the .mdb file can execute any SQL operation on any table. No ABAC, RBAC, or middleware enforcing action-level restrictions.
findings.gap: Cannot restrict an agent to read-only operations on a specific resource type.
findings.recommendation: Build fine-grained RBAC with action-level authorization into the new service layer.

compensating_controls: Deploy API gateway with method-level authorization
Implement application-level permission checks

findings.title: Hardcoded credentials in source code
findings.description: Database credentials are hardcoded as plaintext constants in source code (Private Const DB_PW As String = "crm2005pw"). The credential is committed to the git repository and compiled into the distributed EXE.
findings.gap: Hardcoded credentials in source code. No secrets management, no rotation capability.
findings.recommendation: Migrate credential storage to AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation. Remove hardcoded credentials from source code and git history.

compensating_controls: Rotate the database password immediately
Use environment variables as interim measure

findings.title: No agent identity suspension mechanism
findings.description: No identity management exists. Since there are no agent identities, API keys, or service accounts, there is no mechanism to suspend or revoke a specific agent's access without affecting all users.
findings.gap: Cannot isolate a misbehaving agent without disrupting all users.
findings.recommendation: Implement per-agent API keys with individual revocation when building the API layer.

compensating_controls: Implement per-agent API keys with individual revocation
Use Cognito app clients with per-agent disable

findings.title: No compensation or rollback for write operations
findings.description: No compensation or rollback mechanism exists. The application executes raw INSERT SQL with On Error Resume Next — partial failures are swallowed silently. No saga patterns, no undo endpoints, no compensating transactions.
findings.gap: Multi-step write operations cannot be rolled back. Partial state from failed sequences cannot be compensated.
findings.recommendation: Implement transaction management and compensation patterns when building the service layer.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to RISK-SAFETY: agent_scope=write-enabled but has_http_rpc_surface=false reduces to RISK-SAFETY (no agent-callable multi-step workflows currently exist)
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: STATE-Q1 downgraded from BLOCKER to RISK-SAFETY because has_http_rpc_surface=false — no API surface exists for agents to execute multi-step write workflows. The system is a desktop app with no agent-callable interface.
compensating_controls: Implement database transactions wrapping multi-step operations
Build compensating actions into the new API layer

findings.title: No draft/pending state for agent-proposed writes
findings.description: No draft or pending state exists. The cmdSave_Click handler immediately executes an INSERT into the database with no intermediate review step. All write operations are immediately committed.
findings.gap: No mechanism for an agent to propose a change that a human can review before commitment.
findings.recommendation: Add a status column (DRAFT/CONFIRMED) to enable human-in-the-loop review.

compensating_controls: Implement status enum (DRAFT/PENDING/APPROVED) in Customers table
Build two-step API (create-as-draft, then confirm)

findings.title: No configurable approval gates
findings.description: No approval gates exist. All operations execute immediately without any configurable approval step. No workflow engines, no Step Functions, no human approval tasks.
findings.gap: Cannot configure specific operations to require human approval before execution.
findings.recommendation: Build configurable per-operation approval gates into the new API/service layer.

compensating_controls: Implement operation-level approval flags
Use Step Functions with waitForTaskToken for high-risk operations

findings.title: Customer PII stored without access scoping or differentiation
findings.description: Stage A: Yes — the system stores customer PII (names) and user identifiers. Stage B: B1 — No API exists for response scoping (RISK-SAFETY due to surface-flag downgrade from BLOCKER). B2 — No access differentiation (RISK-SAFETY). B3 — No classification metadata (INFO). Overall: RISK-SAFETY.
findings.gap: No API response scoping, no access control differentiation, no classification metadata for customer PII.
findings.recommendation: Build API response DTOs with field-level filtering and differentiated access scopes for agent vs internal consumers.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to RISK-SAFETY: agent_scope=write-enabled but has_http_rpc_surface=false — no API surface exists to scope responses. B1 downgraded from BLOCKER. Overall severity is RISK-SAFETY (highest of B1-RISK-SAFETY and B2-RISK-SAFETY).
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: DATA-Q1 B1 downgraded from BLOCKER to RISK-SAFETY because has_http_rpc_surface=false — no agent-facing API responses exist to scope. B2 fires as RISK-SAFETY (no access differentiation). Overall: RISK-SAFETY.

b1.reasoning: No API surface exists to scope responses — downgraded from BLOCKER because has_http_rpc_surface=false

b2.reasoning: Single shared database password grants full access to all data — no differentiation

compensating_controls: Build API response DTOs excluding sensitive fields
Implement OAuth scopes separating PII access

findings.title: No schema documentation or versioning
findings.description: No schema documentation, no API contracts, no versioning exists. The database schema is implicit (inferred from SQL statements only). No migration files, no schema registry, no changelog.
findings.gap: No documented or versioned schema. Agent tool bindings would have no stable contract to bind against.
findings.recommendation: Document the database schema and implement API versioning in the new service layer.

compensating_controls: Document current database schema as a starting point
Implement schema versioning when building API layer

findings.title: No input validation — SQL injection vulnerability
findings.description: Zero input validation. User input from txtName.Text is directly concatenated into SQL strings without any validation, sanitization, or parameterization. This creates a SQL injection vulnerability.
findings.gap: No input validation. SQL injection risk. No structured validation error responses.
findings.recommendation: Replace string-concatenated SQL with parameterized queries. Implement input validation with structured error responses.

compensating_controls: Implement parameterized queries immediately
Add input validation middleware in new service layer

findings.title: No sandbox/staging environment
findings.description: No sandbox or staging environment exists. Single production environment with manual deployment (copy EXE to laptops). No Docker compose, no seed data scripts, no environment-specific configurations.
findings.gap: No safe environment to test agent behavior before production.
findings.recommendation: Create a staging environment with production-equivalent data shape when building the service layer.

compensating_controls: Create a copy of the .mdb file for testing
Build Docker-based development environment

findings.title: Zero test coverage
findings.description: No tests exist. README explicitly states 'No tests, no build server; compiled on one developer's machine.' No test files, no test frameworks, no test infrastructure.
findings.gap: Zero test coverage for any functionality.
findings.recommendation: Build comprehensive API test suites (integration tests, contract tests) as part of modernization.

compensating_controls: Write integration tests for critical paths
Implement contract tests for new API endpoints

findings.title: No machine-readable API specification
findings.description: No HTTP/RPC surface — machine-readable spec is not applicable. The system is a desktop application with no callable API surface.
findings.gap: No API surface to describe with a machine-readable specification.
findings.recommendation: Create an OpenAPI 3.0 specification when building the API layer.

findings.title: No structured error responses
findings.description: No HTTP/RPC surface — structured error responses are not applicable. Errors are displayed via MsgBox to desktop users.
findings.gap: No HTTP/RPC surface for structured errors.
findings.recommendation: Implement structured error responses when building the API layer.

findings.title: No idempotent write operations
findings.description: No API endpoints exist for agents to call. Direct database INSERTs have no idempotency mechanism. Surface-flag calibration: has_http_rpc_surface=false — no agent-callable surface.
findings.gap: No idempotency support, but no API surface for agents either.
findings.recommendation: Implement idempotency keys on all write endpoints when building the API layer.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Downgraded to INFO: agent_scope=write-enabled but has_http_rpc_surface=false — no API endpoints exist for agents to call
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: API-Q4 downgraded from conditional BLOCKER to INFO because has_http_rpc_surface=false — no API surface exists for agents to invoke write operations. Idempotency is moot without an API.

findings.title: No identity propagation
findings.description: No identity propagation. System uses Environ("USERNAME") as simple attribution. has_auth_surface=false — system does not issue or enforce identities.
findings.gap: No identity propagation mechanism exists.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2 on-behalf-of flows in the new architecture.

findings.title: No concurrency controls
findings.description: No concurrency controls exist. Access .mdb corrupts monthly under concurrent writes. has_http_rpc_surface=false — no API surface for concurrent agent instances.
findings.gap: No optimistic locking or concurrency management.
findings.recommendation: Implement optimistic locking in the new service layer.

findings.title: No rate limiting — no HTTP surface
findings.description: System exposes no HTTP/RPC surface — API-layer rate limiting is not applicable.
findings.gap: No HTTP/RPC surface for rate limiting.
findings.recommendation: Include API Gateway throttling when building the API layer.

findings.title: No blast radius or transaction limits
findings.description: No transaction limits. Single-record INSERTs with no configurable limits. No HTTP/RPC surface for agents.
findings.gap: No per-agent transaction limits.
findings.recommendation: Build per-agent transaction limits into the new service layer.

findings.title: Data residency — on-premises, minimal PII
findings.description: Data resides on-premises on a single Windows file server. No cross-region replication, no cloud data movement. Minimal PII (customer names and Windows usernames). No sovereignty concerns with current deployment.
findings.gap: No data residency documentation, but on-premises storage has no current sovereignty concerns.
findings.recommendation: Document residency requirements before cloud migration.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to INFO: data is on-premises with minimal PII, no cross-border movement, no sovereignty constraints detected
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: DATA-Q2 resolved to INFO rather than BLOCKER: while agent_scope is write-enabled, the data resides on-premises on a single server with no cross-region replication and minimal PII (customer names). No GDPR/LGPD references, no compliance requirements found.

findings.title: No logging exists — PII-in-logs not applicable
findings.description: System does not log user data and has no logging infrastructure. has_logging_of_user_data=false. PII-in-logs risk is not applicable.
findings.gap: Not applicable — no logging exists.
findings.recommendation: When implementing logging, include PII redaction from the start.

findings.title: No tracing or structured logging
findings.description: No HTTP/RPC surface for agents. No logging or tracing exists at all. has_http_rpc_surface=false — tracing not applicable for desktop app.
findings.gap: No tracing or structured logging, but no agent request path to trace.
findings.recommendation: Implement OpenTelemetry and structured logging in new service architecture.

findings.title: No alerting — no HTTP surface
findings.description: No HTTP/RPC surface. No alerting configuration exists. has_http_rpc_surface=false — alerting on API error rates not applicable.
findings.gap: No alerting, but no API surface to alert on.
findings.recommendation: Configure CloudWatch alarms when building the API layer.

findings.title: No infrastructure governance — no agent-facing surface
findings.description: No HTTP/RPC surface and no auth surface. Desktop app with manual file server administration. No IaC, but no agent-facing integration surface requiring governance.
findings.gap: No IaC, but no agent-facing surface requiring governance.
findings.recommendation: Define all infrastructure as code when building the cloud service.

findings.title: No CI/CD — no HTTP surface
findings.description: No HTTP/RPC surface — API contract testing not applicable. No CI/CD pipeline exists at all.
findings.gap: No CI/CD, but no API to contract-test.
findings.recommendation: Build CI/CD pipeline with API contract testing when creating the service layer.

findings.title: No rollback capability — no deployed HTTP surface
findings.description: No deployed HTTP/RPC surface to roll back. Manual EXE distribution with no deployment automation.
findings.gap: No rollback, but no deployed API surface.
findings.recommendation: Implement blue/green deployment with automatic rollback in cloud architecture.

findings.title: No encryption at rest
findings.description: Access .mdb uses database password (trivial obfuscation, not real encryption). On-premises file format predates modern encryption standards.
findings.gap: No real encryption at rest.
findings.recommendation: Enable KMS encryption on all data stores when migrating to cloud.

findings.title: No selective query support — no API surface
findings.description: No API endpoints exist with pagination/filtering. Desktop application uses direct SQL queries. No HTTP/RPC surface for agents to query.
findings.gap: No pagination/filtering at an API layer.
findings.recommendation: Implement cursor-based pagination and configurable filters on all query endpoints.

evaluations.title: Structured Response Format
evaluations.reason: No API/serialization surface exists — informational signal, no finding emitted.

evaluations.title: Asynchronous Operation Support
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no evidence of operations >30s or long-running workflows.

evaluations.title: Event Emission for State Changes
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no event infrastructure, no message queues, no integration surface in this desktop VB6 app.

evaluations.title: Rate Limit Documentation and Headers
evaluations.reason: No API/HTTP surface exists — informational signal, no finding emitted.

evaluations.title: Queryable Current State
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no agent-queryable API surface exists (desktop app only).

evaluations.title: Circuit Breakers and Resilience
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no external service dependencies (connects only to local file-based database).

evaluations.title: Graceful Degradation Signaling
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no P0 priority provided and not on critical path.

evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no agent-facing API to serve temporal metadata. Now() in INSERT provides creation timestamp but no HTTP surface.

evaluations.reason: No data-quality tooling or data store infrastructure present — informational signal, no finding emitted.

evaluations.reason: Single SQL INSERT uses readable field names (Name, CreatedBy, CreatedOn) but insufficient surface for systematic assessment — informational signal, no finding emitted.

evaluations.reason: No data catalog or metadata surface present — informational signal, no finding emitted.

evaluations.reason: No metrics or telemetry of any kind — informational signal, no finding emitted.

items.summary: Resolve all 3 BLOCKERs (API layer, machine identity, audit logging) and address critical RISK-SAFETY findings (authorization, credentials, rollback, human-in-the-loop, data scoping). Build the foundational API and identity infrastructure.
Implement quality controls: schema versioning, input validation, staging environment, structured errors, observability, CI/CD, and deployment automation for the new service layer.
Build comprehensive test coverage, implement blast radius transaction limits, and ensure encryption at rest for all cloud data stores.

recommended_actions.action: Build REST API service layer to replace direct database access
recommended_actions.rationale: The fundamental blocker is the absence of any API. All other agent readiness controls (auth, audit, rate limiting, etc.) depend on having a callable service layer.

recommended_actions.action: Deploy centralized identity provider with machine identity support
recommended_actions.rationale: Machine identity is required for any agent integration. OAuth2 with client credentials enables per-agent attribution, scoped permissions, and suspension capability.
Write-enabled agents require full audit attribution. CloudTrail + S3 Object Lock provides immutable, tamper-evident logging.

recommended_actions.action: Migrate credentials to AWS Secrets Manager
recommended_actions.rationale: Hardcoded credentials in source code are an immediate security risk. Secrets Manager provides rotation and secure access.

recommended_actions.action: Implement input validation and parameterized queries
recommended_actions.rationale: SQL injection vulnerability must be resolved regardless of agent integration. Parameterized queries are table stakes.
